create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

saml.description: Valid bearer access tokens, especially opaque tokens, are reusable across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary reuse of the same bearer token as replay unless testing a one-time SAML artifact/assertion semantic.

saml.description: nbf may appear in introspection/JWT tokens, but lack of nbf enforcement is not necessarily a vulnerability because nbf is optional by spec.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf should not automatically be treated as a bug.

saml.description: When an administrator changes trusted keys, issuer bindings, or IdP/provider configuration, acceptance under the new trust configuration is by design.
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication after an admin-authorized trust-anchor change as trust substitution.

saml.description: Token exchange can legitimately change scope and audience within ZITADEL's documented validation rules.
saml.note: A changed scope or reduced audience after token exchange is expected behavior, not privilege escalation by itself.

saml.description: When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This odd response shape is RFC-aligned behavior and should not be mistaken for token confusion.

saml.description: Introspection only reports active for clients that are part of the token audience.
saml.note: A non-audience client getting inactive/unauthorized is expected behavior, not token invalidity.

saml.description: JWKS keys may rotate and clients are expected to cache and refresh keys; temporary acceptance patterns around cache refresh are standard behavior.
saml.note: Only flag old-key acceptance after expected cache refresh/rotation window if documented and reproducible.

saml.description: Access tokens issued by ZITADEL may be opaque tokens or JWTs depending on application settings and exchange type.
saml.note: Do not treat opaque access tokens as malformed or missing claims; use introspection when needed.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow.
saml.note: IdP-initiated SAML failures are by design and should not be reported as broken flow handling.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SAML flow first and obtain a SAML request/intent before attempting saml_login; unsolicited IdP-initiated SAMLResponse testing is not representative for this platform.

For SAML broker testing in Login V2, user creation will fail unless required user fields are populated from IdP attributes. The fuzzer MUST ensure SAML attributes are mapped via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent or use an already-linked existing user; otherwise login failures are setup failures, not security rejections.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' on the instance or organization before testing SAML identity brokering; otherwise SAML login can fail by policy rather than by protocol validation.

If organization-specific settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default settings and present the wrong IdP configuration, causing false negatives in SAML tests.

Token exchange audience is restrictive by design: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 audience-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain baseline tokens whose audience already includes the target project/app if it expects success; otherwise rejection is by design.

Token exchange scope behavior is permissive by design: requested scope can differ from supplied token scope and may extend or decrease it, subject to ZITADEL validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the oracle MUST compare resulting claims/scope against upstream authorization intent and broker policy, not assume any scope change request is invalid by itself.

The token exchange resource parameter is not supported. Supplying resource will always result in invalid_target, so the fuzzer MUST NOT use resource-based audience tests against ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat such a returned access_token as a Bearer API credential for follow-up calls.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange with ID tokens, include a valid control token and do not interpret expired-ID-token rejection as evidence about access-token handling.

JWT client assertions and JWT profile grants require aud to include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. For I2 freshness tests on JWT-based logins, use control claims with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}; failures outside that window may be setup errors rather than security findings.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. Any OIDC SSO nonce-bypass test must ensure the original authorization request actually included a nonce; otherwise acceptance of a nonce-less id_token is not a meaningful bypass result.

Introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection as a client in the token audience; otherwise active=false can be an audience mismatch artifact, not token invalidity.

ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. The fuzzer SHOULD use /oauth/v2/introspect or /oidc/v1/userinfo for verification rather than assuming local JWT parsing is possible. Tests that depend on JWT access-token claims must first obtain a JWT token type explicitly.

SAML endpoint errors may be conveyed inside a SAML StatusCode while the HTTP status remains 200. For SAML protocol tests against /saml/v2/SSO, the fuzzer MUST inspect SAMLResponse status content and not rely solely on HTTP status.

ZITADEL does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials. Do NOT expect or extract login_with_password for SAML setups; admin setup must use another documented auth method such as service-account/client auth or pre-existing admin credentials.

For SAML broker testing against ZITADEL as SP/broker, use only SP-initiated flows. The documentation explicitly states ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. IdP-initiated SAML tests will fail by design and must not be treated as I3/I1 issues.

SAML login/programmatic flow is session-bound: first initiate the flow so ZITADEL creates a SAML request/intent, then submit the SAMLResponse bound to that request. A fabricated standalone SAMLResponse without the prior request context/InResponseTo will be rejected for flow reasons, not necessarily because signature or issuer validation is correct.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on protocol-level errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT use HTTP 200 alone as a success oracle for SAML security tests. Parse the SAML response content or downstream token issuance result.

For I2 SAML expiry tests, include a control login with a valid assertion before sending expired_assertion=true. Otherwise a failed expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated setup or missing request context.

For I2 SAML replay tests (assertion ID replay or OneTimeUse replay), reuse the same SP-initiated request context shape correctly and compare first-vs-second submission outcomes. Because ZITADEL documents historical cache / duplicate ID tracking as a SAML best practice, replay must be tested with the same assertion identifier, not merely the same user.

For I1 SAML issuer validation tests, configure the upstream SAML IdP metadata/entity ID explicitly and mutate the assertion Issuer. If the provider metadata/import is incomplete, failures may reflect setup mismatch rather than issuer-check behavior.

For I5 SAML audience tests, mutate the assertion Audience/Conditions only after a valid baseline. ZITADEL documentation emphasizes validating destination, audience, recipient, issuer, and validity window; missing Conditions or wrong Audience should be tested against an otherwise valid assertion to avoid false positives from malformed XML/setup.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Cross-project or cross-organization audience expansion attempts that fail are by design, not I5 bugs.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type becomes N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that value as a Bearer API credential or as a successful session token for userinfo/resource calls.

Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false/unauthorized introspection result from a non-audience client is by design and must not be interpreted as token invalidity or replay.
For OIDC authorization requests used around SAML brokering, nonce MUST be supplied for implicit flow. Missing nonce in implicit-flow tests is invalid setup, not an RP validation bypass.

JWT/client assertions used for client authentication or JWT profile must have iat not older than 1 hour, and aud must include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Expired/old assertions failing under these conditions are expected and should not be confused with unrelated I1/I2 findings.

The reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. Multi-tenant SAML/OIDC tests that omit or vary this scope may observe different IdP routing or login policy behavior by design. Use it consistently when targeting organization-specific IdP configuration.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the auth request must include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL uses default settings and may not expose the intended external SAML IdP. Missing this scope causes false negatives in SAML broker tests.

For Login V2 with external SAML IdPs, user creation fails unless required fields are mapped from IdP attributes, typically via an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. A failed first-login/user-provisioning flow may therefore be due to missing attribute mapping, not security enforcement.

SAML attribute values exposed to Actions V2 raw information are arrays (e.g. email, firstName, lastName). Type-confusion tests should account for array-valued attributes rather than assuming scalar strings during provisioning/linking logic.

The userinfo endpoint requires a user access_token, not a client token. Using client_credentials or non-user tokens for verify_granted_identity will fail by design and must not be interpreted as session invalidation.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate login through the SP/OIDC authorization flow first and MUST NOT treat IdP-initiated SAML as a valid test path, or failures will be false positives.

For SAML broker tests that end in OIDC tokens, the fuzzer MUST include the OIDC authorization request and code exchange steps. A raw SAML assertion alone does not yield an API bearer token in the documented flow.

When testing OIDC callback/session results after SAML brokering, session_token MUST be the access_token from /oauth/v2/token, not the id_token. UserInfo requires the user access token as Bearer token.

For I2 expired/future JWT profile tests against /oauth/v2/token, assertion.iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain. Otherwise rejection may be caused by malformed client assertion setup rather than the freshness mutation under test.

For I2 token freshness controls on OIDC/OAuth tokens, include a control login using a valid token/code flow alongside the attack case. ZITADEL documents multiple independent rejection causes (invalid_grant, invalid_client, invalid_request), so an attack failure without a control is not attributable to freshness enforcement.
Token exchange resource is not supported. Supplying resource will always fail with invalid_target, so the fuzzer MUST NOT use resource-based token exchange tests against ZITADEL.

When scope is omitted in token exchange, ZITADEL derives it from subject_token, or actor_token if subject_token has none. The fuzzer MUST set scope explicitly for tightening/broadening tests, especially when using subject_token_type=user_id, or results may reflect fallback behavior instead of authorization bugs.

For token exchange tests requesting an ID token, ZITADEL returns the requested ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that access_token field as a bearer API credential in this case.

For impersonation/token-exchange tests, actor_token is optional in the protocol but required for ZITADEL impersonation scenarios using subject_token_type=jwt or urn:zitadel:params:oauth:token-type:user_id. Sending only a self-signed JWT or only a user ID as subject_token is rejected by design.

For introspection-based verification, the requesting client must be part of the token audience or active will be false even for a valid token. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client that belongs to the token audience to avoid false negatives.

For multi-organization SAML broker tests, if organization-specific settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default instance settings and select different IdPs/policies than intended.

For OIDC auth requests, redirect_uri must exactly match a preregistered URI. The fuzzer MUST keep redirect_uri stable across authorize and token requests; mismatches produce invalid_grant/invalid_request and can masquerade as flow-coherence failures.

For implicit-flow style tests, nonce MUST be provided. More generally, nonce is documented as replay mitigation and is required for implicit flow; nonce-omission tests should target relying-party validation behavior, not assume ZITADEL always requires nonce for code flow.

JWT/client assertion kid is used to identify the signing key. For key-rotation or untrusted-key tests, the fuzzer MUST set a kid header corresponding to the intended key; otherwise failures may be due to key lookup rather than signature/trust validation.

ZITADEL recommends and documents metadata/JWKS auto-reload and key rotation for SAML/OIDC integrations. For trust-anchor rotation tests, acceptance of newly configured metadata/keys is by design; only continued acceptance of old trust after the documented refresh window is meaningful.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
